title: Components, Intents, and PendingIntent Attack Surface Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies components, intents, and pendingintent attack surface?
options: Expose only necessary capabilities, validate every IPC field and destination, and make delegated intents immutable and narrowly scoped.
Trust intents carrying your package name
Export all components for easier testing
Use one mutable PendingIntent for every notification
questions.answer: Expose only necessary capabilities, validate every IPC field and destination, and make delegated intents immutable and narrowly scoped.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: A PendingIntent is only navigation data and never delegates the creator application’s identity.
questions.explanation: Checking that an incoming Intent is non-null, then forwarding its nested Intent with inherited grant flags, lets an attacker redirect your app’s authority.

questions.prompt: Why can a PendingIntent be security-sensitive?
questions.answer: It lets its holder perform the wrapped operation using the creator application’s identity and permissions.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
